correctness.rationale: In the actual RESULT.md, the merged independent Poisson processes have the identical ordered coupon-label stream. Conditioning on the unique maximum m-th arrival gives the exact binomial mixture and integral law for K; with b solving n Q_m(b)=1, the Gamma-tail hazard Q_m(b)/f_m(b) is asymptotic to b/(b-m) uniformly on the Gumbel window because (b-m)^2/b tends to infinity. The mark ratio p_m/Q_m is asymptotic to b/m-1; conditional binomial-to-Poisson mixing with e^{-G}~Exp(1) yields Geom(1/(1+a)) for A->a, while mean/variance control yields K/A->Exp(1) for A->infinity. The Gamma large-deviation rate I(r)=r-1-log r identifies the m/log n regimes, with no monotonicity assumption. Finite examples check the conditional law but do not prove it.

The Nov 2 marked-shortage theorem explicitly examines a deterministic near-cutoff draw count N_n(x), with independent deficiency marks; it does not give the random stopping-time K law or process-level convergence.

value.rationale: The number of minimally filled types exactly at the random common m-coverage time is a natural stopped-occupancy statistic, distinct from the stopping clock and from deterministic-time deficiencies. Its full geometric family, exponential normalization and logarithmic quota threshold give a usable phase classification for generalized coupon collection, beyond the known fixed-m singleton result.

limitations: Uniform iid labels only; no moment convergence or uniform rates claimed.
m=1 finite distribution is known; novelty concerns arbitrary growing m_n random-stopped marks.
Subsequential limit statement does not classify arbitrary nonconvergent A_n beyond its limit points.
